questions.question:
You intend to deploy several Azure virtual machines.  
  
You need to control which ports Internet devices can use to access the virtual machines.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) role

questions.explanation:
A network security group (NSG) uses inbound security rules to allow or deny traffic to Azure virtual machines by source, destination, port, and protocol. An NSG can be associated with a virtual machine network interface or its subnet to restrict Internet access to approved ports.\
\
**Learn more:** [How network security groups filter network traffic](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/network-security-group-how-it-works)

questions.question: What should a desktop application use to communicate with Azure and manage resources?
questions.explanation:
Azure Resource Manager REST APIs provide the programmatic interface an application uses to create, update, query, and delete Azure resources. ARM templates are declarative deployment files, while Azure CLI and Azure Cloud Shell are interactive command environments.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage Azure resources by using the REST API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/manage-resources-rest) · [What is Azure Resource Manager?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has an on-premises network containing multiple servers.  
  
The company intends to reduce these administrative responsibilities:  
  
- Backing up application data  
- Replacing failed server hardware  
- Managing physical server security  
- Updating server operating systems  
- Managing permissions to shared documents  
  
The company plans to migrate the servers to Azure virtual machines.  
  
You need to identify which administrative responsibilities will be eliminated after the planned migration.  
  
Which two responsibilities should you identify? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Azure virtual machines are infrastructure as a service (IaaS). Microsoft manages the physical hosts and physical datacenters, including physical security, while the customer remains responsible for the guest operating system, data, and identities and permissions.

**Learn more:** [Shared responsibility in the cloud - Microsoft Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/shared-responsibility)

questions.question: Which Azure service offers serverless computing?
questions.explanation: Azure Functions provides serverless compute, allowing code to run in response to events without provisioning or managing servers.

Azure management groups provide a governance scope above subscriptions. Governance conditions applied to a management group are inherited by its associated subscriptions, enabling centralized management of access, policies, and compliance across multiple subscriptions.

**Learn more:** [Manage your Azure subscriptions at scale with management groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/management-groups/manage)

questions.question: Which Azure service should be used to store certificates?
questions.explanation:
Azure Key Vault securely stores and manages certificates, including X.509 certificates and associated private keys.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Key Vault certificates documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/certificates/)

questions.question:
Solution: You intend to require Azure Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure MFA requires users to complete an additional verification method during sign-in. It increases account security but does not provide an identity-migration approach that minimizes the user impact of retiring the on-premises Active Directory environment.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enable per-user Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication to secure sign-in events](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-mfa-userstates)

questions.question:
Solution: You intend to synchronize all Active Directory user accounts with Azure Active Directory (Azure AD).  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Directory synchronization provisions on-premises Active Directory identities into Microsoft Entra ID and supports a common identity for cloud resources. With password hash synchronization, users can continue using their existing on-premises password in the cloud, reducing disruption during the migration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Directory synchronization with Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/architecture/sync-directory) · [What is Microsoft Entra Connect and Connect Health?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/whatis-azure-ad-connect)

questions.question:
You intend to provision Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) resources in Azure.  
  
Which resource is an example of IaaS?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Machines are an Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) offering: Azure provides the underlying physical infrastructure, while the customer manages the guest operating system and applications. Azure App Service and Azure SQL Database are Platform as a Service (PaaS) offerings.\
\
**Learn more:** [Fundamentals of Azure for On-Premises Experts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/migration/migrate-from-on-premises-fundamentals)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
Where can you find information about the personal data Microsoft collects, how Microsoft uses that data, and the purposes for which the data is used?
questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Privacy Statement is Microsoft’s privacy notice. It describes the personal data Microsoft collects, how it uses and processes that data, and the purposes for its use.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Privacy Statement](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/privacy/privacystatement)

questions.question: Which cloud model has all hardware resources owned by a third party and shared among multiple tenants?
questions.explanation:
A public cloud is owned and operated by a third-party provider and uses shared underlying infrastructure for multiple customers or tenants. Private clouds dedicate infrastructure to one organization, while hybrid clouds combine cloud environments.\
\
**Learn more:** [Isolation in the Azure public cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/isolation-choices)

questions.question: What does an Azure Service Level Agreement (SLA) guarantee for virtual machines?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Virtual Machines SLA defines an availability commitment, expressed as an uptime percentage under specified deployment conditions. It does not guarantee bandwidth, performance, or the availability of individual features.\
\
**Learn more:** [Reliability in Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/reliability-virtual-machines)

questions.question:
Solution: You recommend using Microsoft Managed Desktop.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Managed Desktop manages supported Windows endpoint devices and their configuration, updates, and security; it does not automate the repeated deployment and removal of custom Azure virtual machines. It also does not support the required mix of Windows Server 2016 and Ubuntu Linux virtual machines. Microsoft Managed Desktop reached end of service on July 31, 2024.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Microsoft Managed Desktop?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/managed-desktop/overview/service-plan)

questions.question:
Solution: You recommend using Azure DevTest Labs.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure DevTest Labs reduces administration for short-lived development and test environments by supporting repeatable VM deployment through custom images, formulas, and templates. It also supports expiration dates that automatically delete lab VMs, making it suitable for recurring deployment and removal of Windows Server 2016 and Ubuntu Linux virtual machines.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure DevTest Labs concepts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devtest-labs/devtest-lab-concepts) · [Create and manage ARM templates for VMs in DevTest Labs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devtest-labs/devtest-lab-use-resource-manager-template)

questions.question:
Solution: You recommend using Azure Reserved Virtual Machine (VM) Instances.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Reserved VM Instances provide a billing discount in exchange for a one-year or three-year commitment and do not affect resource runtime operations. They do not automate the deployment or removal of short-lived virtual machines; an automation service such as Azure Automation would be needed to reduce that administrative work.\
\
**Learn more:** [What are Azure Reservations?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/reservations/save-compute-costs-reservations)

questions.question:
Solution: Deploy the virtual machines to two or more scale sets.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
A scale set by itself does not protect against a datacenter failure. Datacenter resiliency requires virtual machines to be distributed across availability zones, or separate zonal resources with appropriate traffic routing and failover.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machine-scale-sets/overview) · [Reliability in Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/reliability-virtual-machine-scale-sets)

questions.question:
Solution: Deploy the virtual machines across two or more regions.  
  
Does this fulfill the goal?
questions.explanation:
Deploying workloads in multiple Azure regions provides redundancy beyond a single data center, so a data-center failure in one region does not affect the virtual machines deployed in another region.\
\
**Learn more:** [Regions and zones on Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/aws-professional/regions-zones)

questions.question:
Solution: You change a DDoS protection plan.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
An Azure DDoS Protection plan mitigates DDoS attacks for protected public IP resources; it does not configure a virtual machine for inbound HTTP access from the Internet. HTTP exposure requires suitable public connectivity and inbound network rules.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure DDoS Protection overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ddos-protection/ddos-protection-overview)

questions.question:
Solution: You change an Azure firewall.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Firewall can publish a web server for inbound Internet access by using a DNAT rule to translate the firewall’s public IP address and HTTP port to the virtual machine’s private IP address and port. The corresponding translated traffic is allowed, enabling HTTP access to VM1.\
\
**Learn more:** [Filter inbound Internet traffic with Azure Firewall DNAT using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/tutorial-firewall-dnat) · [Azure Firewall rule processing logic](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/rule-processing)

questions.question:
Solution: You deploy the virtual machines across two or more availability zones.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure availability zones are physically separate datacenter locations in a region with independent power, cooling, and networking. Distributing virtual machines across two or more zones provides resilience when a single datacenter or zone fails.\
\
**Learn more:** [What are Azure availability zones?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/availability-zones-overview) · [Create virtual machines in an availability zone using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/create-portal-availability-zone)

questions.question:
Solution: You deploy the virtual machines across two or more resource groups.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure resource groups organize and manage resources but do not determine their physical datacenter placement. Protection from a single datacenter failure requires deploying the workload across multiple availability zones, which are physically separate datacenter groups with independent infrastructure.\
\
**Learn more:** [What are Azure availability zones?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/azure/reliability/availability-zones-overview) · [Architecture Strategies for Using Availability Zones and Regions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/design-guides/regions-availability-zones)

questions.question:
Solution: You change an Azure Traffic Manager profile.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Traffic Manager provides DNS-based routing to endpoints that are already Internet-facing; clients connect directly to the selected endpoint. Changing a Traffic Manager profile alone does not provide VM1 with public HTTP connectivity or permit HTTP traffic to it.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Traffic Manager FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/traffic-manager/traffic-manager-faqs)

questions.question:
Solution: Modify a network security group (NSG).  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
A network security group can allow inbound TCP traffic on port 80 from the Internet to a virtual machine by using an inbound security rule. Azure NSGs filter inbound traffic at the subnet or network-interface level; without a matching allow rule, the default inbound deny rule blocks it.\
\
**Learn more:** [How network security groups filter network traffic](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/network-security-group-how-it-works)

questions.question:
Solution: You use the Azure portal.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Azure portal runs in supported modern browsers on tablet devices, and it provides a browser-based interface for creating Azure virtual machines.\
\
**Learn more:** [Supported browsers and devices for Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-portal/azure-portal-supported-browsers-devices) · [Quickstart: Create a Windows virtual machine in the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/quick-create-portal)

questions.question:
Solution: Use PowerShell in Azure Cloud Shell.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Cloud Shell provides an authenticated, browser-accessible PowerShell environment for managing Azure resources, including from the Azure mobile app. Azure PowerShell can create a virtual machine by using the `New-AzVM` cmdlet.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use Cloud Shell in the Azure mobile app](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-portal/mobile-app/cloud-shell) · [Quickstart: Create a Windows virtual machine in Azure with PowerShell](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/quick-create-powershell)

questions.question:
Solution: You use Bash in Azure Cloud Shell.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Cloud Shell provides an authenticated terminal that supports Bash, and Azure CLI commands can create and manage Azure virtual machines. Cloud Shell is available through the Azure mobile app, allowing Azure resources to be managed from a mobile device.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use Cloud Shell in the Azure mobile app](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-portal/mobile-app/cloud-shell) · [Quickstart: Create a Windows VM using the Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/quick-create-cli)

questions.question:
Solution: You use the PowerApps portal.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
The PowerApps portal does not provide Azure virtual-machine provisioning. Azure virtual machines are created through Azure management interfaces such as the Azure portal, which provides the VM creation workflow.\
\
**Learn more:** [Quickstart: Create a Windows virtual machine in the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/quick-create-portal)

questions.question:
Solution: You deploy the VMs to a scale set.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
A Virtual Machine Scale Set protects against a datacenter-level failure only when its instances are deployed across multiple availability zones. A scale set without a multi-zone configuration does not provide that guarantee and can experience downtime during a zone failure.\
\
**Learn more:** [Reliability in Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/reliability-virtual-machine-scale-sets)

questions.question: What is used to grant access permissions to Azure Virtual Desktop resources?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop uses Azure role-based access control (RBAC) to control access to resources. Roles are assigned to users or administrators and grant the permissions required for specific tasks.\
\
**Learn more:** [Built-in Azure RBAC roles for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/rbac)

questions.question:
Your company intends to deploy several web servers and several database servers in Azure.  
  
You need to recommend an Azure solution that limits the types of connections from the web servers to the database servers.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Azure network security groups (NSGs) use security rules to allow or deny inbound and outbound traffic by source, destination, port, and protocol. Associating appropriate NSGs with the web and database server subnets or network interfaces restricts the permitted web-to-database connections.\
\
**Learn more:** [How network security groups filter network traffic](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/network-security-group-how-it-works)

questions.question: How many data copies does an Azure Storage account using locally redundant storage (LRS) maintain?
questions.explanation: Locally redundant storage (LRS) synchronously replicates data three times within a single physical location in the primary region.

questions.question:
You have an Azure Sentinel workspace.  
  
You need to automate responses to threats that Azure Sentinel detects.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: adaptive network hardening in Azure Security Center
adaptive application controls in Azure Security Center

questions.explanation: While the technically correct tool for automating threat responses in Azure Sentinel is Playbooks (which is not among the choices), Azure Monitor Workbooks is the closest available option and is commonly cited in Azure learning materials for Sentinel automation. Workbooks provide visualization and can be integrated with automation workflows, though Playbooks (Logic Apps) are the primary automation mechanism.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of vertical scaling in a cloud environment?

options.text: adding an additional CPU to an existing Azure virtual machine
adding an additional Azure virtual machine
adding an additional Azure Virtual Desktop session host
adding an additional Azure App Service instance automatically

questions.explanation:
Vertical scaling increases the capacity of an existing virtual machine, such as by adding CPU resources. Microsoft documents VM scale-up as changing the VM size to obtain more CPU, memory, or storage capacity.\
\
**Learn more:** [Resize a virtual machine - Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/sizes/resize-vm)

questions.question: How many data copies does geo-zone-redundant storage retain?
questions.explanation:
Geo-zone-redundant storage maintains three copies across availability zones in the primary region and three locally redundant copies in the secondary region, for a total of six copies.\
\
**Learn more:** [Data redundancy - Azure Storage | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-redundancy)

questions.question: What should be used to prevent traffic from an Azure virtual network from being routed to an Azure Storage account through the internet?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Storage service endpoint routes supported Azure Storage traffic directly from the virtual network subnet over the Microsoft Azure backbone network, avoiding the public internet.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure virtual network service endpoints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-service-endpoints-overview) · [Restrict network access to PaaS resources with virtual network service endpoints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/tutorial-restrict-network-access-to-resources)

questions.question: Which Azure service can be used as a security information and event management (SIEM) solution?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel is a cloud-native SIEM solution that collects and analyzes security data and supports threat detection, investigation, response, and proactive hunting.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Microsoft Sentinel SIEM?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/overview)

You need to recommend the Azure service that will minimize the administrative effort needed to deploy and remove the virtual machines.  
  
What should you recommend?
questions.explanation:
Azure DevTest Labs is intended to create, use, and manage development and test virtual machines. questions.question:
This item requires you to evaluate the underlined text to decide whether it is correct.  
  
The Azure Standard support plan is the lowest-cost option for receiving 24x7 access to support engineers by phone.  
  
Instructions: Review the underlined text. If it makes the statement correct, select `No change is needed`. If the statement is incorrect, select the answer choice that makes the statement correct.
questions.explanation:
The Azure Standard plan is the least expensive paid Azure support plan that provides 24x7 access to technical support by email, phone, and chat after a support request is submitted. The lower-cost Developer plan provides support-engineer access only during business hours through prioritized Microsoft Q&A responses.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Support Plans Comparison](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/support/plans/)

questions.question:
You have an on-premises network containing several servers.  
  
You plan to migrate every server to Azure. You need to recommend a solution that ensures some servers remain available if a single Azure datacenter is offline for an extended period.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation: Fault tolerance uses redundancy so that a service can continue operating when a component or site fails, including an extended outage of one Azure datacenter.

questions.question:
Your company has an Azure subscription that includes the following unused resources:  
  
- 20 user accounts in Azure Active Directory (Azure AD)  
- Five groups in Azure AD  
- 10 public IP addresses  
- 10 network interfaces  
  
You need to reduce the company's Azure costs.  
  
Which unused resources should you remove?
questions.explanation:
Azure public IP addresses can generate charges based on their SKU and allocation type; static or reserved addresses can be billed even when unused. Azure AD users, Azure AD groups, and network interfaces do not have a standalone resource charge of this kind.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure IP Addresses pricing](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/ip-addresses/)

questions.question:
You need to identify the type of failure that an Azure Availability Zone can be used to protect access to Azure services from.  
  
What should you identify?
questions.explanation:
Azure Availability Zones distribute resources across physically separate datacenters within a single Azure region. Their independent infrastructure provides resiliency to a datacenter failure; protection from an Azure region failure requires a multi-region design.\
\
**Learn more:** [What are Azure availability zones?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/availability-zones-overview) · [Redundancy, replication, and backup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/concept-redundancy-replication-backup)

questions.question:
Your company has an Azure subscription that includes several resources.  
  
You need to determine which department is responsible for the cost of each resource.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure tags can be applied to resources with metadata such as a Department or CostCenter value, allowing costs to be grouped and attributed by department in Azure Cost Management. Budgets define spending limits, while alerts provide notifications.\
\
**Learn more:** [Group and allocate costs using tag inheritance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/costs/enable-tag-inheritance) · [Use tags to organize your Azure resources and management hierarchy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/tag-resources)

questions.question:
Which two features or services can integrate with Azure Monitor? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
> NOTE: Each correct answer is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Application Insights is Azure Monitor’s application-monitoring capability, while Log Analytics provides the workspace and query experience for Azure Monitor log data. Workspace-based Application Insights integrates with a Log Analytics workspace to store and analyze telemetry.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and configure Application Insights resources — Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/create-workspace-resource) · [Azure Monitor data sources and data collection methods](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/azure/azure-monitor/fundamentals/data-sources)

questions.question:
You have an on-premises network that includes 100 servers.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that gives your users additional resources. The solution must minimize capital and operational expenditure costs.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: a complete migration to the public cloud

questions.explanation: A hybrid cloud extends the existing on-premises infrastructure with scalable cloud resources. It avoids the capital expense and operational overhead of a new data center while allowing the organization to use additional resources as needed.

questions.question: What should an application connect to in order to obtain security tokens?
questions.explanation:
Azure Active Directory (now part of Microsoft Entra ID) is the identity platform that authenticates identities and issues security tokens, including access, refresh, and ID tokens, to applications.\
\
**Learn more:** [Tokens and claims overview - Microsoft identity platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/security-tokens)

questions.question:
Which two characteristics describe the public cloud? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Public-cloud resources are available for customers to provision and manage on demand, and their usage is measured for pay-as-you-go billing. Public cloud does not inherently require dedicated hardware, unsecured connectivity, or limited storage.\
\
**Learn more:** [AWS Cloud Essentials](https://aws.amazon.com/getting-started/cloud-essentials/)

questions.question:
You need to migrate an on-premises server using a lift-and-shift migration.  
  
To what type of cloud service should you migrate?
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as a service (IaaS) provides cloud virtual machines and related infrastructure, enabling an existing server workload to be moved with minimal changes. This is the standard lift-and-shift migration model.

questions.question:
You have on-premises servers that run Windows Server.  
  
What should you implement to manage the servers through the Azure portal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Arc-enabled servers connects on-premises Windows Server machines to Azure so they can be managed as Azure resources in the Azure portal.\
\
**Learn more:** [Cloud-native server management with Azure Arc-enabled servers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-arc/servers/cloud-native/overview)

questions.question: Which term describes increasing a virtual machine’s computing capacity by adding memory or CPUs?
questions.explanation: Vertical scaling increases the resources of a single virtual machine, such as its CPU cores or memory.

Azure Key Vault securely stores and controls access to secrets, including passwords and other administrative credentials. Azure Resource Manager deployments can retrieve secrets from a key vault rather than exposing the credential value in deployment artifacts.

questions.question:
You need to gather and automatically analyze security events from Azure Active Directory (Azure AD).  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel is a cloud-native SIEM and SOAR service that collects Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) security data and automatically analyzes it to detect, investigate, and respond to threats.\
\
**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Configure security analytics for Azure AD B2C data with Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory-b2c/configure-security-analytics-sentinel)

questions.question:
You have an Azure web app.  
  
You need to manage the web app’s settings from an iPhone.  
  
Which two Azure management tools can you use? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Azure Cloud Shell provides a browser-accessible, authenticated terminal for managing Azure resources, and the Azure portal is accessible through a web browser. Both can therefore be used from an iPhone to manage web app settings.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Azure Cloud Shell?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-shell/overview) · [What is the Azure mobile app?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-portal/mobile-app/overview)

questions.question:
Your company intends to begin using Azure and migrate all of its network resources to Azure.  
  
You need to begin the planning process by exploring Azure.  
  
What should you create first?
questions.explanation:
An Azure subscription provides the boundary for billing, access, and resource deployment. Resource groups and virtual networks are created within a subscription, and management groups are used to organize subscriptions. [What is Azure Resource Manager?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/overview)\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Azure Resource Manager?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/overview)

questions.question: Microsoft 365 is an example of which cloud service model?
questions.explanation: Software as a service (SaaS) provides complete, provider-managed applications to users over the internet. Microsoft 365 is a suite of such applications.

questions.question:
A company hosts virtual machines (VMs) in Microsoft Azure. The VMs reside in a single Azure virtual network named VNet1.  
  
The company has users who work remotely and need access to the VMs in VNet1.  
  
You need to enable access for the remote workers.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure DirectAccess on a Windows Server 2012 server VM.

questions.explanation:
An Azure Point-to-Site (P2S) VPN creates a secure connection from an individual remote client computer to an Azure virtual network, making it appropriate for remote users who need to access VMs in VNet1.\
\
**Learn more:** [About Azure Point-to-Site VPN connections](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/point-to-site-about) · [About Azure VPN Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/vpn-gateway-about-vpngateways)

questions.question:
Your company has an Azure subscription containing resources across several regions.  
  
You need to create the Azure resource required to meet the policy requirement.  
  
What should you create?
questions.explanation:
Azure Policy defines and assigns governance rules that enforce organizational standards and assess compliance across Azure resources and scopes, including resources in multiple regions.\
\
**Learn more:** [Overview of Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/overview)

questions.question:

You need to create the Azure resource required to meet the policy requirement.  
  
What should you create?
questions.explanation:
AWS Basic Support is included for all AWS customers and therefore has the lowest cost. It includes documentation and best-practice guides, service health checks and alerts, plus 24/7 access for account and billing questions.

questions.question: Which service offers a unified way to project and manage non-Azure resources in Azure Resource Manager (ARM)?
questions.explanation:
Azure Arc projects existing non-Azure and on-premises resources into Azure Resource Manager, enabling centralized Azure-based management and governance across hybrid and multicloud environments.\

**Learn more:** [Azure Arc overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-arc/overview)

questions.question:
You have an Azure virtual machine named VM1.  
  
You plan to encrypt VM1 by using Azure Disk Encryption. Which Azure resource must you create first?
questions.explanation:
Azure Disk Encryption requires an Azure Key Vault to store and manage the disk-encryption keys and secrets used by the virtual machine. A key encryption key can optionally be created inside that vault for additional protection, but the Key Vault itself is the required resource.\
\
**Learn more:** [Creating and configuring a key vault for Azure Disk Encryption](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/linux/disk-encryption-key-vault)

Azure costs vary with the selected service tier or SKU and the Azure region in which the resource is deployed. Data egress is also a billing factor: outbound-transfer charges commonly depend on the amount of data transferred, while inbound transfer is generally free. Azure cost-optimization guidance identifies location and egress data as billing factors, and Microsoft documents that metered data transfer charges outbound data while inbound transfer is free.

questions.question:
You have an Azure Storage account named `storage1`.  
  
You need to make sure that containers can be created in `storage1`, but cannot be deleted from it.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a ReadOnly lock for storage1.
Create a delete lock for storage1.

questions.explanation: A Delete (CanNotDelete) management lock allows authorized users to create and modify resources while blocking deletion. This meets the requirement to allow container creation but prevent deletion. ReadOnly locks would prevent creation entirely, and soft-delete options provide recovery rather than preventing deletion.

questions.question: Which service can automatically restore a resource lock after the lock has been removed?
questions.explanation:
Azure Blueprints enforces blueprint resource locks through Azure RBAC deny assignments created for the blueprint assignment. The lock protection is managed as part of that assignment, allowing it to be reapplied if it is removed.\
\
**Learn more:** [Understand resource locking in Azure Blueprints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/blueprints/concepts/resource-locking)

questions.question:
Your company has 10 departments. The company intends to implement an Azure environment.  
  
You need to make sure that every department can use a separate payment option for the Azure services it consumes. What should you create for each department?
questions.explanation:
An Azure subscription provides a billing boundary for consumed Azure services and is associated with the payment method or billing arrangement used for those charges. Separate subscriptions therefore allow each department’s consumption to use a different payment option.\
\
**Learn more:** [Supported payment methods for Azure subscriptions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/manage/supported-payment-methods)

questions.question:
Which two advantages does cloud computing provide? Each correct answer represents a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: enables the rapid provisioning of resources
has the same configuration options as on-premises
shifts capital expenditures (CAPEX) to operating expenditures (OPEX)

questions.explanation: Cloud computing enables resources to be provisioned rapidly on demand. Its pay-as-you-go consumption model also shifts costs from upfront capital expenditures (CAPEX) to operating expenditures (OPEX).

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783700918247-3me8cau7.png)  
  
How should the composite SLA for the application be calculated?
questions.explanation:
For dependent services on a single critical path, the composite SLA is calculated by multiplying each service SLA. Therefore, 99.9% × 99.99% equals 99.89001%. Microsoft’s Cloud Adoption Framework expresses the single-region composite SLA as the product of the SLA for every service on the critical path.\
\
**Learn more:** [Protect your Azure cloud estate - Cloud Adoption Framework](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/manage/protect)

questions.question:
Solution: Include a local network gateway in your strategy.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A local network gateway represents a remote VPN device and its network address space for site-to-site VPN connectivity. It does not enforce rules for traffic between Azure web servers and database servers; network security groups are used to control permitted traffic flows.\
\
**Learn more:** [Reliability in Azure Virtual Network Gateways](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/reliability-virtual-network-gateway)

questions.question:
Solution: You add network security groups (NSGs) to your strategy.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure network security groups control inbound and outbound traffic through allow and deny rules that can specify the source, destination, port, and protocol. Applying NSGs to the relevant web-server and database-server subnets or network interfaces can therefore control the connection types between those server tiers.\
\
**Learn more:** [How network security groups filter network traffic](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/network-security-group-how-it-works)

questions.question:
You need notification when Microsoft intends to perform maintenance that could affect resources deployed in an Azure subscription.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Service Health provides subscription-specific notifications and alerts for planned maintenance that might affect Azure resources.\
\
**Learn more:** [Planned maintenance overview - Azure Service Health](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-health/service-health-planned-maintenance) · [What is Azure Service Health?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-health/overview)

questions.question:
Solution: You configure the use of Azure AD Identity Protection.  
  
Does this solution satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID Protection (Azure AD Identity Protection) evaluates sign-ins from unfamiliar or anonymous IP addresses as user/sign-in risk, and its risk-based policies can be configured to remediate that risk by requiring a secure password change, not only MFA or blocked access. Because Identity Protection natively supports triggering a forced password change when a risky sign-in condition such as an unidentified IP is detected, configuring it satisfies the stated goal.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Identity Protection - Microsoft Entra ID Protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-protection/overview-identity-protection)

questions.question:
Solution: You configure Azure AD Privileged Identity Management.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure AD Privileged Identity Management manages and governs privileged role access, such as just-in-time elevation. It does not detect sign-ins from unidentified IP addresses or require users to change passwords. Microsoft Entra ID Protection risk-based policies can require a secure password change to remediate detected user risk.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-configure) · [Microsoft Entra ID Protection risk-based access policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-protection/concept-identity-protection-policies)

Your company operates datacenters in Los Angeles and New York and has a Microsoft Azure subscription.  
  
You are configuring the two datacenters as geo-clustered sites to provide site resiliency.  
  
You need to recommend an Azure storage redundancy option. The data storage requirements are:  
  
- Data must be stored across multiple nodes.  
- Data must be stored on nodes in distinct geographic locations.  
- Data must be readable from the secondary location as well as the primary location.  
  
Which Azure storage redundancy option should you recommend?
questions.explanation:
Read-access geo-redundant storage (RA-GRS) maintains redundant copies in a geographically separate secondary region and permits reads from that secondary endpoint as well as the primary endpoint. Standard geo-redundant storage replicates geographically but does not allow secondary-region read access; zone-redundant and locally redundant storage do not provide geographic replication.

**Learn more:** [Azure Storage redundancy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-redundancy)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You intend to store 20 TB of data in Azure. The data will be accessed infrequently and visualized by using Microsoft Power BI.

questions.question: Which additional resource does an Azure virtual machine require?
questions.explanation:
An Azure virtual machine must be connected through a network interface to a subnet in an Azure virtual network. A public IP address is optional, while service endpoints and Azure Firewall are optional networking features.\
\
**Learn more:** [Virtual networks and virtual machines in Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/network-overview) · [Create, change, or delete a network interface](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-network-interface)

questions.question: At which layer of the OSI model does ExpressRoute operate?
questions.explanation:
Azure ExpressRoute provides Layer 3 network connectivity between on-premises networks and the Microsoft cloud, using BGP to exchange routes. [Azure ExpressRoute Overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/expressroute/expressroute-introduction)\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure ExpressRoute Overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/expressroute/expressroute-introduction)

questions.question: How many data copies are maintained by an Azure Storage account that uses geo-redundant storage (GRS)?
questions.explanation:
Azure geo-redundant storage (GRS) stores three copies in the primary region and asynchronously replicates data to three copies in a secondary region, maintaining six copies in total.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Storage redundancy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-redundancy)

questions.question: Which service supplies network-traffic filtering across multiple Azure subscriptions and virtual networks?
questions.explanation:
Azure Firewall provides centralized, stateful network and application-level traffic filtering across subscriptions and virtual networks. It supports a hub-and-spoke design in which traffic from multiple spoke virtual networks is routed through a central firewall.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Firewall FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/firewall-faq) · [What is Azure Firewall?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/overview)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that includes a resource group named RG1.  
  
Users must **not** be able to perform these operations:  
  
- Delete RG1.  
- Modify resources in RG1.  
- Delete resources from RG1.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Apply a delete lock to RG1.
Apply a read-only lock to RG1.
Grant role-based access control (RBAC) permissions to RG1.

questions.explanation:
A read-only management lock at the resource-group scope is inherited by resources in that group and permits only read operations. It prevents updates and deletions of both the resource group and its resources; a delete lock would still permit modifications.\
\
**Learn more:** [Lock your Azure resources to protect your infrastructure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/lock-resources)

questions.question:
Your company intends to automate server deployments to Azure.  
  
Your manager is worried that administrative credentials could be exposed during deployment.  
  
You need to recommend an Azure solution that encrypts the administrative credentials during deployment. What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Azure Key Vault securely stores and manages secrets such as administrative passwords, allowing deployment processes to retrieve credentials without exposing them in deployment files or scripts.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Key Vault Keys, Secrets, and Certificates Overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/about-keys-secrets-certificates)

questions.question:
You have 50 virtual machines hosted on-premises and 50 virtual machines hosted in Azure. The on-premises virtual machines connect with the Azure virtual machines.  
  
Which cloud model type is this?
questions.explanation:
A hybrid cloud combines on-premises infrastructure with public-cloud services such as Azure, with the environments working together through connectivity.\
\
**Learn more:** [Hosting applications on Azure — Hybrid cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/developer/intro/hosting-apps-on-azure)

questions.question: What can you use to automatically send an alert when an administrator stops an Azure virtual machine?

questions.question: What is the maximum term available when purchasing Azure Reserved VM instances?
questions.explanation: Azure Reserved VM Instances are offered with fixed commitment terms of one year or three years. The maximum available term is three years, providing the longest commitment period for cost savings.

questions.question:

questions.explanation:

\

questions.question: Where does Azure Monitor retain event data?

questions.question: What should you use to assess whether your company’s Azure environment complies with regulatory requirements?

questions.question: What is the most serious failure that an Azure Availability Zone can protect access to an Azure service from?
questions.explanation:

questions.question: What can Azure Information Protection encrypt?

questions.question:
You have an accounting application named App1 that uses a legacy database.  
  
You plan to migrate App1 to the cloud.  
  
Which service model should you use?
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as a service (IaaS) provides virtualized compute infrastructure on which an existing legacy application and its legacy database can be hosted with the required operating-system and database control. PaaS generally requires adapting the application to a managed platform, while SaaS is a finished application service.

questions.question:
Solution: You recommend including management groups in the strategy.  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure management groups organize subscriptions and apply inherited governance, policy, and access controls at scale; they do not automatically provision Azure resources. A resource-deployment automation mechanism is required to create the identical resources for each business unit.\
\
**Learn more:** [Organize your resources with management groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/management-groups/overview)

questions.question:
Solution: You recommend including the Azure API Management service in the strategy.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure API Management is a platform for managing, securing, and publishing APIs, rather than a service for automatically provisioning identical Azure resource sets. Repeatable automated Azure resource deployments are implemented with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Bicep or Azure Resource Manager templates.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure API Management - Overview and Key Concepts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-key-concepts) · [What is Azure Resource Manager?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/overview)

questions.question:
Solution: You recommend including Azure Resource Manager templates in the strategy.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Resource Manager templates define Azure infrastructure declaratively and can be deployed repeatedly to produce consistent resource configurations. A single template can therefore automate creation of the identical required Azure resources for each business unit.\
\
**Learn more:** [Templates overview - Azure Resource Manager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/templates/overview?view=migrate-classic)

questions.question:
Your company operates 10 offices and plans to create several billing reports in the Azure portal. Each report will include the Azure resource utilization for every office.  
  
Which Azure Resource Manager feature should you use before creating the reports?
questions.explanation:
Azure resource tags provide key-value metadata that categorizes resources by organizational context, such as an office. Applying an office tag to each resource enables billing and cost data to be grouped, filtered, and reported by office.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use tags to organize your Azure resources and management hierarchy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/tag-resources)

questions.question: Which cloud models support deployment of physical servers?

options.text: private cloud and hybrid cloud only
private cloud, hybrid cloud and public cloud

questions.explanation: Physical servers can be deployed in a private cloud and may be integrated with public-cloud services as part of a hybrid cloud. They are not deployed into a public cloud, where the provider owns and operates the underlying physical infrastructure.

Solution: You create an Azure App Service and Azure Storage accounts.

**Learn more:** [Best practices for secure PaaS deployments](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/paas-deployments) · [Secure your Azure App Service deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-security)

questions.question:
Solution: You create Azure virtual machines, Azure SQL databases, and Azure Storage accounts.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure virtual machines are Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), not Platform as a Service (PaaS). Therefore, an environment that includes virtual machines does not comply with a requirement to use only PaaS solutions.\
\
**Learn more:** [Security best practices for IaaS workloads in Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/iaas) · [What is the Azure SQL Database service?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/sql-database-paas-overview?view=azuresql)

questions.question:
Solution: You create an Azure App Service and Azure SQL databases.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure App Service provides a PaaS environment for hosting applications, and Azure SQL Database is a PaaS database service. Both resources therefore meet a migration requirement that only PaaS solutions be used.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure App Service documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/) · [What Is Azure SQL?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/azure-sql-iaas-vs-paas-what-is-overview?view=azuresql)

questions.question:
Solution: You create an Azure App Service and Azure virtual machines with Microsoft SQL Server installed.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure App Service is a PaaS offering, whereas Azure Virtual Machines are IaaS and require management of the guest operating system and installed SQL Server. A solution containing those virtual machines does not meet a requirement to use only PaaS services.\
\
**Learn more:** [Fundamentals of Azure for On-Premises Experts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/migration/migrate-from-on-premises-fundamentals) · [Azure App Service documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/)

questions.question: Which cloud service model requires the least management responsibility from the customer?
questions.explanation: Software as a service (SaaS) minimizes customer management responsibility because the provider operates and maintains the application, platform, and underlying infrastructure.

Which Azure service should you use in the Azure portal to view service-failure notifications that could affect VM1?

Azure Service Health provides subscription- and region-specific notifications about Azure service incidents that can affect resources. Azure Monitor is the listed portal service used to access and manage these service health notifications and alerts.\

**Learn more:** [Azure Service Health notifications overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Azure/service-health/service-health-notifications-properties) · [Azure Service Health documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-health/)

An Azure administrator intends to run a PowerShell script that creates Azure resources.  
  
You need to recommend the computer configurations that can be used to run the script.  
  
Which three computers can run the script? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: a computer that runs macOS and has PowerShell Core 6.0 installed.
a computer that runs Windows 10 and has the Azure PowerShell module installed.
a computer that runs Linux and has the Azure PowerShell module installed.
a computer that runs Linux and has the Azure CLI tools installed.
a computer that runs Chrome OS and uses Azure Cloud Shell.

questions.explanation:
Azure PowerShell requires the Az PowerShell module, which is supported on Windows and Linux. Azure Cloud Shell has the Az PowerShell module preinstalled, so it can run Azure PowerShell scripts from a Chrome OS device. PowerShell Core without the Azure PowerShell module and Azure CLI alone do not provide the required Azure PowerShell cmdlets.

**Learn more:** [How to install Azure PowerShell](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/azure/install-azure-powershell?view=azps-16.0.0)

questions.question:
You need to buy a third-party virtual security appliance to deploy in an Azure subscription.  
  
What should you use?

Azure Marketplace provides third-party virtual machine and network virtual appliance offerings, including security appliances, that can be purchased and deployed into an Azure subscription.\

questions.question:

What should you use?

questions.question:
Solution: Your strategy includes two virtual machines and a single availability zone.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A 99.99% Azure VM availability commitment requires two or more VM instances distributed across two or more Availability Zones in the same Azure region. Two VMs in only one availability zone do not provide protection from a zone failure.\
\
**Learn more:** [Overview of virtual machines in Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/overview)

questions.question:
Solution: You add two virtual machines and two availability zones to your strategy.  
  
Does the solution achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure provides a 99.99% virtual-machine connectivity SLA when two or more VM instances are deployed across two or more availability zones in the same Azure region. Two VMs distributed across two zones meet that requirement with the minimum number of VMs and zones.\
\
**Learn more:** [Overview of virtual machines in Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/overview)

questions.question:
Solution: Your strategy includes one virtual machine and two availability zones.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A 99.99% Azure VM availability commitment across availability zones requires two or more VM instances distributed across two or more availability zones in the same Azure region. One virtual machine cannot provide a redundant instance in another zone, so the design does not meet the required availability level.\
\
**Learn more:** [Overview of virtual machines in Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/overview)

questions.question: Which Azure service offers a set of version-control tools for managing code?
questions.explanation:
Azure Repos provides version-control tools for managing code, including Git and Team Foundation Version Control (TFVC).\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Azure Repos?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/get-started/what-is-repos?view=azure-devops)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You intend to deploy several Azure virtual machines.  
  
You must ensure that the services hosted on the virtual machines stay available if a single data center fails.  
  
What are two possible solutions? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.

options.text: Deploy the virtual machines to two or more availability zones.
Deploy the virtual machines to two or more resource groups.
Deploy the virtual machines to a scale set.
Deploy the virtual machines to two or more regions.

questions.explanation:
Availability zones are physically separate datacenter groups with independent power, cooling, and networking, so deploying replicated virtual machines across two or more zones protects the workload from the loss of one datacenter. Virtual Machine Scale Sets provide a managed, load-balanced group of VM instances and support high-availability deployments, including spreading instances across availability zones. Resource groups do not provide failure isolation, and merely placing VMs in different regions does not by itself configure replication, routing, or failover.

**Learn more:** [What are Azure availability zones?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/availability-zones-overview) · [Availability options for Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/availability)

questions.question: With which Azure support plans can you create a new support request?

options.text: Premier, Professional Direct, and Standard only
Premier, Professional Direct, Standard, and Developer only
Premier, Professional Direct, Standard, Developer, and Basic

questions.explanation:
Azure provides support requests for subscription management, billing, and quota adjustments at every support level, including Basic. Paid Developer, Standard, Professional Direct, and Premier plans additionally provide technical-support entitlements at their respective service levels.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create an Azure support request](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-portal/supportability/how-to-create-azure-support-request) · [Request quota increases and get support](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/synapse-analytics/sql-data-warehouse/sql-data-warehouse-get-started-create-support-ticket)

questions.question:
Solution: Recommend a Professional Direct support plan.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Professional Direct support includes access to technical support by email and phone after a support request is submitted, satisfying a requirement for an option to access support engineers by either method.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Support Plans Comparison](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/plans/)

questions.question:
Solution: Recommend a Premier support plan.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
A Premier support plan provides technical support with the ability to specify Email or Phone as the preferred contact method for an Azure support request, satisfying a requirement to access support engineers through either channel.\
\
**Learn more:** [How to create an Azure support request - Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-portal/supportability/how-to-create-azure-support-request)

questions.question:
Solution: Recommend a Basic support plan.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Basic does not include access to technical support engineers by email or phone after a support request is submitted. That access is available with higher support plans, so Basic cannot meet a policy requiring phone or email access to support engineers.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Support Plans Comparison](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/support/plans/)

questions.question:
Solution: Recommend a Standard support plan.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Azure Standard support plan provides 24x7 access to technical support by email, phone, and chat after a support request is submitted, meeting a requirement for access to support engineers by phone or email.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Support Plans Comparison](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/support/plans/)

questions.question: What can be used to identify Azure virtual machines that are underutilized or unused?
questions.explanation:
Azure Advisor analyzes virtual-machine utilization and generates cost recommendations to resize or shut down underutilized or unused instances.\
\
**Learn more:** [Optimize virtual machine spend by resizing or shutting down underutilized instances - Azure Advisor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/advisor/advisor-cost-recommendations)

questions.question:
Which two customer types are eligible to use Azure Government to build a cloud solution? Each correct answer represents a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Azure Government is intended for U.S. federal, state, and local government customers and their partners, subject to eligibility validation. Accordingly, a United States government entity and a United States government contractor are eligible customer types.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Azure Government?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-government/documentation-government-welcome)

questions.question:
Solution: You delete the unused network interfaces.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure network interfaces are not billed independently, so deleting unused network interfaces does not reduce Azure costs. Unused public IP addresses can be billable, but they are not removed by this solution.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create, change, or delete a network interface](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-network-interface)

questions.question:
Solution: You delete the unused user accounts.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID Free includes user and group management at no cost. With no paid licenses or separately billed identity services stated, deleting unused user accounts does not reduce Azure costs.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra ID Free](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/manage/microsoft-entra-id-free)

questions.question:
Solution: You remove the unused groups.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID’s free edition includes user and group management. Unused Microsoft Entra ID groups do not incur the Azure resource charges associated with billable resources such as public IP addresses, so deleting the groups does not reduce Azure costs.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory)](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/active-directory/)

questions.question:
Solution: Remove the unused public IP addresses.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation: Unused Azure public IP addresses can generate charges. Deleting public IP addresses that are no longer needed reduces those costs.

options.text: Use Bash in Azure Cloud Shell.
Use PowerShell in Azure Cloud Shell.

questions.explanation:
The Azure portal is browser-based and supports creating virtual machines. Azure Cloud Shell is browser-accessible, available from mobile devices, and provides both Bash and PowerShell environments for managing Azure resources, including deploying virtual machines.

**Learn more:** [What is Azure Cloud Shell?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-shell/overview) · [Quickstart: Create a Windows virtual machine in the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/quick-create-portal)

questions.question:
You need to launch Azure Cloud Shell.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Cloud Shell is launched from the Azure portal by selecting the Cloud Shell icon. Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell are the command environments that Cloud Shell provides, while an ARM template is for deploying Azure resources.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Learn: Quickstart for Bash in Azure Cloud Shell](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-shell/quickstart)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to create a virtual machine.  
  
Where in Azure will the virtual machine be located?
questions.explanation: An Azure virtual machine is an Azure Resource Manager resource and must be deployed to a resource group within an Azure subscription.

questions.question:
Your developers have created 10 web applications that must be hosted on Azure.  
  
You need to determine which Azure web tier plan should host the web apps. The web tier plan must meet these requirements:  
  
- The web apps will use custom domains.  
- The web apps each require 10 GB of storage.  
- The web apps must each run on dedicated compute instances.  
- Load balancing between instances must be included.  
- Costs must be minimized.  
  
Which web tier plan should you use?
questions.explanation: The Standard tier is the minimum App Service tier that meets all requirements: it supports custom domains, provides 50 GB storage (exceeding 10 GB per app), offers dedicated compute instances, includes load balancing, and is the most cost-effective tier meeting all criteria. Basic tier lacks built-in load balancing and supports only 3 dedicated instances.

questions.question:

What is one advantage of using a public cloud service for the servers instead of an on-premises network?

options.text: The public cloud is owned by the public, NOT a private corporation

questions.question: Which cloud-computing benefit ensures that users can continuously access a cloud-based application with minimal downtime?
questions.explanation: High availability is the design goal of keeping an application accessible despite failures or maintenance, minimizing service interruptions and downtime.

questions.question: Which cloud-computing model incorporates both on-premises and cloud-based resources?
questions.explanation: A hybrid cloud combines on-premises resources with cloud-based resources, allowing them to operate together.

questions.question: What is the initial stage of the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure?

questions.question:
Your company intends to migrate several servers to Azure.  
  
The company’s compliance policy requires that a server named FinServer be located on a separate network segment.  
  
You are assessing which Azure services can meet the compliance-policy requirements.  
  
Which Azure solution should you recommend?

options.text: a resource group for FinServer and another resource group for all the other servers
a virtual network for FinServer and another virtual network for all the other servers
a VPN for FinServer and a virtual network gateway for each other server
one resource group for all the servers and a resource lock for FinServer

questions.explanation: Azure virtual networks provide logically isolated network segments. Placing FinServer in one virtual network and all other servers in another virtual network satisfies the requirement for a separate network segment.

questions.question:
Solution: You recommend that the company subscribe to the Professional Direct support plan.  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation: General architecture guidance for assessing an Azure environment's design is already available under the Standard support plan, which costs less than Professional Direct. Because the stated goal explicitly requires keeping expenses to a minimum, recommending the pricier Professional Direct plan is not the most cost-effective way to satisfy the requirement.

questions.question:
Solution: You should use Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS).  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation: Azure Virtual Machines are an Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) offering, providing virtualized compute resources for deploying and managing virtual machines.

questions.question:
Solution: You should use Software as a Service (SaaS).  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Machines are an Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) offering; SaaS is intended for consuming ready-made applications rather than deploying virtual-machine infrastructure.\
\
**Learn more:** [Fundamentals of Azure for On-Premises Experts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/migration/migrate-from-on-premises-fundamentals)

questions.question:
Solution: You should use Platform as a Service (PaaS).  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation: Azure virtual machines are provided through Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), which supplies virtualized compute infrastructure. Platform as a Service (PaaS) is intended for deploying and managing applications without managing the underlying virtual machines, so it is not the appropriate cloud deployment solution for deploying Azure virtual machines.

questions.question:
Solution: You intend to use several Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) directories.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Multiple Microsoft Entra tenants add provisioning, security, governance, and cross-tenant management complexity. Azure supports delegated, segmented administration of divisions' resources within a single tenant by using management groups, subscriptions, resource groups, and Azure RBAC, which minimizes administrative effort.\
\
**Learn more:** [Secure resource isolation in a single tenant in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/architecture/secure-single-tenant) · [Resource isolation with multiple tenants to secure with Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/architecture/secure-multiple-tenants)

questions.question: For a software as a service (SaaS) cloud service, which responsibility is shared by Microsoft and the customer?
questions.explanation:
Identity and directory infrastructure management is shared in SaaS: Microsoft operates the underlying identity service infrastructure, while the customer configures and manages users, access, and identity-related controls. Microsoft manages the SaaS application and underlying operating systems; customers retain responsibility for their data.\
\
**Learn more:** [Shared responsibility in the cloud - Microsoft Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/shared-responsibility)

questions.question: Which Azure service should be used to collect events from multiple resources in a centralized repository?
questions.explanation:
Azure Event Hubs provides centralized, high-throughput ingestion for event data from many producers and retains the event stream so it can be consumed by downstream services. Azure Monitor analyzes monitoring telemetry, Azure Stream Analytics processes event streams, and Azure Analysis Services supports analytical data models.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Event Hubs documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-hubs/event-hubs-about)

questions.question:
